Ta voiture automatique avait déjà des vi: Your automatic car already had gears. The only difference is that here, you're the one who changes them.
Elle a <b>des vitesses elle aussi</b>, s: It has gears too, usually between 4 and 8. A little computer picks the right one and changes it for you. When you're stopped, a part called the “torque converter” does the clutch's job: that's why it never stalled.
Le moteur, lui, ne change pas : il tourn: The engine itself doesn't change: it's always turning when it's on (at least ~800 rpm at idle), and it's comfortable between 1,500 and 4,500 rpm. You choose the gear to keep it in that zone, and your left foot replaces the converter.

<b>Et à l'arrêt ?</b> Les roues sont imm: And when you're stopped? The wheels aren't moving, but the engine has to keep turning. So you need a way to disconnect the engine from the wheels: that's the clutch's job. In an automatic, the converter did that all by itself. If you don't separate them, the wheels hold the engine back and it chokes: that's stalling.
C'est LA notion à comprendre. Le reste e: This is THE thing to understand. Everything else follows from it.
<b>Pédale enfoncée</b><span>Les disques: Pedal pressedThe discs are apart. The engine turns on its own, the wheels don't move.
<b>Pédale enfoncée (« débrayé ») :</b> m: Pedal pressed (“clutch in”): engine and wheels are separated. You can stop or change gear without stalling.
<b>Point de patinage :</b> les disques c: Biting point: the discs start to rub. The car begins to creep forward, and the engine slows a little (the sound drops). This is where you need to be slow and gentle.
<b>Pédale relâchée (« embrayé ») :</b> t: Pedal released (“clutch out”): everything turns together. You can take your left foot off completely.
<b>Le secret pour ne pas caler :</b> rel: The secret to not stalling: lift the pedal quickly up to the biting point, slowly through the biting point, then normally once the car is moving.

<b>Pied gauche = embrayage, et rien d'au: Left foot = clutch, and nothing else. Never brake with your left foot.
<b>Toujours enfoncer l'embrayage à fond<: Always press the clutch all the way down to change gear or start the engine.
<b>Ne laisse pas ton pied posé dessus</b: Don't rest your foot on it while driving: it wears the clutch out. Put your foot to the left of the pedal, on the floor.

<span class=\"f-front\"><b>Il n'y a pas: There's no P positiontap to readTo park: handbrake firmly on, then switch off the engine with a gear engaged (1st uphill, reverse downhill). Remember to go back to neutral before starting again.

<span class=\"f-front\"><b>Pour doubler,: To overtake, you shift down yourselftap to readIn the automatic, flooring it made it drop a gear by itself. Here, if the car lacks pick-up, shift down a gear (from 5th to 4th, or from 4th to 3rd), then accelerate.
<span class=\"f-front\"><b>Le frein mote: You choose the engine brakingtap to readThe lower the gear, the more the car slows down when you lift your foot. On a long downhill, a lower gear holds the car back without overheating the brakes.
